movie.title: A Working Man
movie.overview: Levon Cade left behind a decorated military career in the black ops to live a simple life working construction. But when his boss's daughter, who is like family to him, is taken by human traffickers, his search to bring her home uncovers a world of corruption far greater than he ever could have imagined.

reviews.author: Manuel São Bento
reviews.content:
FULL SPOILER-FREE REVIEW @ https://fandomwire.com/a-working-man-review/

"A Working Man is a textbook example of a movie that fails in every fundamental aspect of its own genre.

Without impactful action sequences, engaging characters, or any valid attempt at innovation or narrative depth, David Ayer delivers a frustratingly generic, utterly forgettable experience.

Jason Statham does his best to elevate a project doomed from the first draft of the script, but not even his charismatic presence can save a film that will inevitably end as one of the worst of the year."

Rating: D

reviews.author: r96sk
reviews.content: 'A Working Man' is imperfectly very good. I do have a couple of issues with it, but all in all I have to say that I did enjoy this to a fairly strong degree. Jason Statham seldom disappoints in an action thriller, I'm a fan of his so was always likely to get the required fun out of this. Statham is great, naturally without him the movie would be vastly less entertaining. Away from the former British diver (still can't quite believe that's the same guy!), there are too many characters - which is one of the issues I have. There didn't need to be so many peeps in this. Even so, those onscreen are all decent enough and none register as overt negatives in my mind. David Harbour does well in a small role, he usually speaks the same way in roles but this feels minorly different. Michael Peña and Arianna Rivas are solid, as is Jason Flemyng. The latter's character should've be the only bad guy in this, or at least one of a few. He gives enough that we didn't need anyone else in my opinion, especially as 'higher-ups' Andrej Kaminsky and Maximilian Osinski give weaker performances. Chidi Ajufo is the best of the rest. My other issue lies with the run time. I guess with so many characters it did need to be almost two hours in length, however you could've told this story within 90 minutes without a doubt. But again, as noticeable as that and the other issue is, it at least doesn't hinder much for me.

reviews.author: MovieGuys
reviews.content:
"A working Man" is an accidental satire, of the US action film genre.

Working class guy, who served in the military and now works for a migrant families construction company, looks to save their angelic daughter, the vision of perfection, from the evil Russian human traffickers. 

Everything is an exaggeration. From the notion of the working class guy, a rough diamond, a patriot,  with a heart of gold. The migrant family with the dutiful, over achiever on steroids daughter, the true inheritors of the American dream. Even, the minimum wage construction workers, who are told to make sure they "keep their fingers" (you can see occupational health and safety is a big thing) are so happy they look like they belong in the original production of "Snow White" (the real one, not the hideous remake). As for the Russians, well surprise, surprise, they are brutal, cruel and stupid. No one saw that coming, right?

I won't mix words, this is cliched, biased, condescending, pro Western military, jingoistic, crap. Interesting too, how venture capitalists "State Street" make a brief appearance, in the opening scenes. If they thought this would lift their profile, well all I can say is it didn't "do it, for me". Sorry guys. 

Is there an upside? In short no. Even the action has a ham fisted, "seen it all before", air of stale, stagnation, about it. 

In summary, a horrible facsimile of superior action films, you have probably seen before. Loaded down with trite cliches, stereotypes and jarring biases. One to avoid.

reviews.author: Louisa Moore - Screen Zealots
reviews.content:
On paper, director David Ayer‘s revenge action thriller “A Working Man” should be a slam dunk for Jason Statham. Based on Chuck Dixon’s novel “Levon’s Trade,” it has all the familiar elements that not only cater to the actor’s strengths, but also to the desires of his most die hard fans. Unfortunately, very little about the film works, and it comes across as dull, predictable, and unmemorable.

Levon (Statham) is a former black ops solider turned construction worker who is forced to return to his lethal past when his boss’s daughter (Arianna Rivas) is abducted by human traffickers. What starts as a rescue mission soon unravels a deeper web of corruption, pushing Levon to do what he does best: take down bad guys with ruthless efficiency.

The premise is well-worn but serviceable, but never quite rises above its own mediocrity. The stunt work is strong and the fights are bloody, but the action sequences mostly lack the punch and creativity needed to garner any feelings of excitement. The action is middling, which makes the uninspired story stand out in the worst way.

Even worse, the film lacks personality. It’s competently made but painfully generic, with a by-the-numbers plot that fails to generate any real emotional stakes. The script (co-written by Ayer and Sylvester Stallone) doesn’t do enough to elevate the material beyond standard action fare.

Despite being well cast, the film wastes a terrific supporting turn from David Harbour, and it feels like the reliable tough guy Statham is running on autopilot. Nobody enjoys watching a movie where the lead actor is delivering a performance that feels more like a contractual obligation than a passion project.

Working in harmony with Ayer’s directorial style, Shawn White’s cinematography proves to be the brightest spot. This is a polished, good looking action thriller, at least visually speaking.

If I had to sum up “A Working Man” in one word, it would be “serviceable.” This is a film that will be buried under Statham’s long list of similar (and much better) movies.

By: Louisa Moore / SCREEN ZEALOTS

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Well if you just thought Jason Statham was going to make a movie about the dangers of the construction industry then the first few scenes will put you straight and give a clue that his past is altogether more violent. That is going to come in handy when the daughter of his boss is kidnapped-to-order by some people traffickers and he is, initially reluctantly, drafted into track her down. With consummate ease, he sets about his task facing down some of the menacing Russian brotherhood who rule the roost supplying girls, drugs and booze to whoever can afford to pay! Can he find the girl? Will the sun come up? There’s not the slightest hint of jeopardy to any of this derivative outing for a star whose usual charisma has been left in his Winnebago. It’s got bits of “Die Hard” (1988) mixed in with, I thought, that Clint Eastwood “Cry Macho” (2021) affair plus the seriously camped up pairing of Jason Flemyng and Maximilian Osinski to make sure that any scintilla of credibility was well and truly throttled after about fifteen minutes of this repetitive and predictable drama. Sylvester Stallone had an hand in the writing - I suppose someone had to put the full stops in the script, and David Ayer shows little, is any, flair as the thing lumbers along for what seems like a lot longer than two hours. Let’s hope Jace isn’t going down the Bruce Willis boulevard of broken dreams here, and doesn’t make any more duds like this.

reviews.author: Dean
reviews.content: Was really good. Jason's movies never disappoint.

reviews.author: Dark Jedi
reviews.content:
I was fairly sure that I would like this movie. For starters it is a Statham movie and I almost always like Statham but, in addition, the ever so useless “critics” at the rotten site wrote it down (the audience gave it 87% fresh).

It is a pretty conventional action movie with elements from a lot of previous action movies. It has the usual bits in it like the lone very kick-ass hero, a kidnapped daughter, some mafia guys and other assorted criminals to beat up in various ways and plenty of guns and things that goes boom.

It is never going to win any rewards for its script, acting or realism. That is fine with me. This movie takes all the good elements that an action movie should have and strings them together into a very entertaining action roller coaster.

In short, it is a very Statham movie.

The action is great and they did not try to do some nonsense like going for a PG rating which is a relief. It is of course not very plausible from time to time but not so ridiculously far out as in the last couple of John Wick movies.

The story is decent and works well to serve as a foundation for the action scenes. After all, the main reason to watch a Statham movie is to watch Statham beat up, shot up or blow up the bad guys after all.

So overall, for me, this is a solid four star movie. A movie made to entertain without any of the usual Hollywood rubbish in it (which is probably why woke tomatoes wrote it down).

reviews.author: Dr Nostromo
reviews.content:
72/100

An ex-special forces soldier is now working as a foreman when his boss' daughter is kidnapped. Time to go get her. There is absolutely nothing original here. But, if you like watching Jason Statham doing his thing, something my wife and I enjoy immensely, you'll have a great time with it. It's a well made film full of colorful characters, some good lines and lots of action that isn't trying to be deep or complicated ...just entertaining. Considering the ratings, I think many have forgotten that sometimes a movie doesn't need to be a masterpiece to be fun. - DrNostromo.com

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: When his boss's daughter is kidnapped by human traffickers, a former black ops soldier abandons his peaceful construction job to rescue her and dismantle a vast corrupt network.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Levon Cade traded his high-stakes black ops career for a quiet life working in construction, hoping to leave violence behind forever. However, his peaceful existence is shattered when his employer's daughter, whom he treats like family, is abducted by a ruthless human trafficking syndicate. Forced to resurrect his deadly military skills, Levon embarks on a relentless search to bring her back safely. Along the way, he exposes a web of deep-seated corruption far more dangerous and expansive than he ever anticipated.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Levon Cade is an ex-black ops operative who has retired from elite military service to live a low-profile life as a construction worker. He values his newfound quiet and close bonds with his work crew, especially his boss and his boss's young daughter, Jenny. Tranquility turns to chaos when Jenny is suddenly snatched by a sinister human trafficking ring operating in the shadows. Realizing law enforcement cannot act fast enough, Levon activates his dormant skills and lethal training to track down her captors. His investigation leads him from back-alley criminal hideouts to high-end establishments fronting illegal operations. As he fights his way through various levels of the syndicate, Levon uncovers chilling evidence that influential figures outside the underworld are enabling the trade. Each violent confrontation brings him closer to Jenny while deepening the complexity of the rescue mission. Armed with unmatched tactic proficiency and unyielding determination, he prepares for a final showdown against a entrenched system of crime and corruption.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: A Working Man is an action-thriller following Levon Cade, a retired black ops operative seeking solace in a simple construction job. When his boss's daughter is abducted by human traffickers, Levon is forced to utilize his formidable tactical background to rescue her. His journey takes him deep into a dark underworld, revealing a sprawling network of institutional corruption that reaches far beyond the street-level cartel.

story_structure.climax: Levon launches a high-stakes, violent raid on the syndicate's main stronghold, confronting the network's leadership in a final showdown to rescue the young woman.
story_structure.conflict: When his employer and friend's teenage daughter is kidnapped by a human trafficking network, Levon agrees to step back into the dangerous world he abandoned to locate and save her.
story_structure.resolution: With the daughter safely returned home and the criminal conspiracy dismantled, Levon completes his rescue mission and steps back toward his quiet life with his own family.
story_structure.introduction: Former black ops operative Levon Cade attempts to put his deadly past behind him, seeking a quiet, normal life as a construction foreman while striving to be a good father to his daughter.
story_structure.risingAction: Levon utilizes his specialized military skills and connections to track down the kidnappers, dismantling low-level operatives, fighting through violent enforcers, and discovering that the trafficking ring is part of a much larger web of systemic corruption.
